One World Trade Center. Also known as the Freedom Tower, this 94-story supertall skyscraper was completed in 2014 in lower Manhattan, rising 1,776 feet including its spire. Symbolizing American resilience and renewal, it occupies the primary site of the former World Trade Center destroyed on September 11, 2001. Designed by architect David Childs of Skidmore, Owings and Merrill, the tower's height of 1,776 feet references the year of American independence. The spire rises 408 feet above the roof, making it one of the tallest structures in the Western Hemisphere and a dominant feature of the Manhattan skyline. The tower houses office space, the 9/11 Memorial and Museum at the base, and the One World Observatory on the one-hundredth and one-hundred-first floors. The facade uses prismatic glass to reflect light and the sky, symbolizing transparency and openness, while the reflective quality creates a dynamic appearance throughout the day. It incorporates extensive security features and sustainability measures, including LED lighting and wind turbines, reflecting twenty-first-century building standards. Its completion marked the closure of a decade-long memorial period and the economic revitalization of lower Manhattan.
